terra.problem: Moses does mention the sword in Deuteronomy 20:13, so saying he never says a word about swords overstates the point.
Moses does describe a city refusing peace and waging war in Deuteronomy 20:12. The explanation overstates the passage by saying he does not say what the enemy will do at all.
The passage places the priest's address before the officers' address, but does not say his is the first voice the soldiers hear.
The final sentence leaves out the condition that the new house has not been dedicated. It makes the instruction sound as though it applies to any man with a new house.
Being pledged does not establish that the man and woman have met. The passage does not say whether they have.
The passage does include the priest's address telling the army not to be afraid or fainthearted. Saying there is no speech about being brave overlooks that address.
The contrast in verses 16–18 concerns cities of the nations the LORD is giving Israel as an inheritance. Saying the nearby nations are a different case broadens that category.
The different command applies to cities of the nations the LORD is giving Israel as an inheritance, not explicitly to every city of the nearby nations.
